subject: Mutual Action Plan — Quickstart: service accounts, org seed, safelist & VPC peering window
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Sims <emma.sims@synapsehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-11 09:14 PDT
Subject: Mutual Action Plan — Quickstart: service accounts, org seed, safelist & VPC peering window

Emma —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation I pulled together a compact mutual action checklist so we can get Synapse running on a production-like evaluation environment in a 2-week sprint. High level asks below; I attached a one-page checklist (MAP-Quickstart-Checklist.xlsx) with owners and target dates.

Summary (target: provisioned test org + keys + safelist + peering in 10 business days):
- Org seed: we need a Synapse tenant admin to accept the org invite and confirm SAML SSO settings (step 1).
- Service accounts and API keys: Redwood will create two service accounts for eval (one read-only, one full-generate). Synapse needs to approve key TTL and rotation policy.
- IP safelist: provide 3 CIDR ranges (or single NAT egress IPs) for our eval cluster. We can accept IPv4 /32 single IPs if you use static NAT.
- VPC peering (optional for throughput testing): request acceptance window of 48 hours once we initiate peering.

Immediate asks for your team this week:
1) Reply with the admin email to accept the Redwood org invite.
2) Send the NAT egress IPs or CIDR ranges for the safelist (format: 203.0.113.45/32 or 198.51.100.0/24).
3) Confirm if you want VPC peering for the eval (we'll send peering request and a CloudFormation snippet).

Notes on keys: we plan to use ephemeral keys for session-based tests (TTL=6 hours) and a long-lived key for CI (rotate every 30 days). If your security team requires HSM/KMS reference, we can provide the KMS key-id and signing policy.

If this looks good I’ll upload the MAP to the shared Drive and create the HubSpot milestone.

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP-Quickstart-Checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan — Quickstart: service accounts, org seed, safelist & VPC peering window

Karthik —

Appreciate the clear list. We want to proceed with the 2-week sprint. Quick answers inline: 
1) Admin to accept invite: emma.sims@synapsehealth.com (I will accept today).
2) NAT egress IPs: our infra team confirmed two static egress IPs: 198.51.100.45/32 and 198.51.100.46/32. We can also open a /28 if you need a block but prefer single IPs to keep firewall rules minimal.
3) VPC peering: yes, we want to enable peering for throughput validation — please schedule peering request next Wednesday (2027-04-14).

Security note: our compliance team asked about logging retention for the eval. Can Redwood provide a pointer to how long request traces are retained and how to extract per-tenant logs?

Emma
Director, Product
Synapse Health

Subject: RE: Mutual Action Plan — Quickstart: service accounts, org seed, safelist & VPC peering window

Hi Emma + team —

Thanks for the quick confirmation. A few operational details from infra that make the peering and safelist step straightforward: 

IP safelist guidance (what we need from Synapse):
- Preferred: provide static egress IPs as /32 entries (you already provided 198.51.100.45/32 and .46/32). We will add these to the eval tenant allowlist.
- Alternative: a CIDR block (e.g., 198.51.100.0/28) if you prefer to manage fewer rules.

VPC peering steps (summary):
1) We will open a peering request from our eval VPC and share the peering ID and the exact route table changes.
2) Synapse to accept the peering and add two route table entries to point to our peer CIDR (we’ll provide the CloudFormation snippet).
3) Security groups: allow outbound TCP 443 to our service IPs, and inbound rules from our peer CIDRs to your test subnets.
4) Acceptance window: please accept within 48 hours of the request to avoid rekey/refresh work on our end.

Service accounts & keys: 
- We will create two service accounts in the seeded org: redwood-eval-readonly@redwood, redwood-eval-generator@redwood.
- For ephemeral sessions we recommend TTL=6h. If your policy needs <6h, tell us and we’ll adjust; if you need longer-lived keys for CI, we will provision a restricted CI key rotated every 30 days.

Logging & retention: 
- For the eval environment we retain request traces for 14 days by default. We can enable a 30-day retention for this tenant for the trial window (requires config flag; we’ll toggle once you sign off).

Next steps:
- Karthik to send the DocuSign for the MAP acknowledgement (simple one-pager).
- We will create the peering request on 2027-04-14 morning PT and send the acceptance link.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Infrastructure Ops
Redwood Inference

Emma / Synapse IT —

Great — thanks for the details and for accepting the invite, Emma. A few confirmations and timeline: 
- I uploaded an editable MAP sheet to Drive (link in metadata) and created a HubSpot milestone for the 2-week sprint.
- We will create the service accounts and provisional keys once the org invite is accepted (ETA: today EOD).
- Neha will open the peering request on 2027-04-14 09:00 PT. Please watch for the acceptance link; the request will expire after 48 hours.
- I attached the DocuSign to formalize the MAP; can you please route to procurement? The DocuSign is a short acknowledgement (no financial commitment) that documents the target dates.

Open items for Synapse: 
- Confirm logging retention change to 30 days for the trial (reply here).
- Confirm who on your side will accept the peering (name & email).

If you prefer, we can also run a 30-minute ops handoff call on Thursday to walk your infra team through the CloudFormation snippet and SG/route changes — suggest 2027-04-15 10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Karthik
